notes.meaning: Leaders of the Levite families came to Joshua, Eleazar the high priest, and tribal leaders at Shiloh. They asked for the living spaces and grazing lands God had promised them through Moses. The Levites had patiently waited until the other tribes received their land before asking for their own share.

differ.view: The other tribes had grown careless and neglected the Levites until the Levites stepped forward to plead their own case.
The Levites were not forgotten; their request simply came in proper order after the other tribes knew what territory they had to share.

notes.meaning: The tribes of Israel gladly obeyed the Lord and gave up some of their own towns and surrounding pastures to the Levites. No tribe complained about sharing what they had received. Caring for God's ministers was treated as an offering directly to the Lord.

The very first lot was drawn for the Kohathite clan, specifically for Aaron's descendants who served as priests. They were given thirteen towns from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin. God in His providence placed the priests in the territory that would later surround Jerusalem, where the temple would one day stand.

The rest of the Kohathite clan, who were ordinary Levites rather than priests, received ten towns. These towns were drawn from the tribes of Ephraim, Dan, and the western half of Manasseh. This kept Aaron's wider family situated close to the priests.

The Gershonite clan received thirteen towns in the northern and eastern lands of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and eastern Manasseh. The Merarite clan received twelve towns from Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun. In total, all forty-eight towns promised through Moses were divided among the three main branches of Levi.

Israel distributed all forty-eight towns and their open grazing lands by lot, just as God had commanded Moses. Scattering the Levites among all the tribes turned an old curse into a blessing, because it placed teachers of God's law across the entire nation. It allowed every ordinary Israelite to have spiritual help close to home.

Judah and Simeon provided specific towns by name to the family of Aaron, because their lot was drawn first. Simeon is listed with Judah because Simeon's territory was located entirely inside Judah's borders. The priests were honored with the first selection because of their sacred calling before God.

The priests received the ancient city of Hebron and the grazing land around its walls. Caleb kept the surrounding farming fields and outlying villages as his own family inheritance. Caleb gave up the town itself without complaint so God's priests would have a place to dwell.

differ.view: The Levites were the true owners and proprietors of the cities given to them, not merely guest tenants.
The Levites held rights only to certain houses and pasture, while other Israelites continued to live in and share the cities.

notes.meaning: Hebron was handed over to the priests along with its nearby grasslands, serving also as a safe refuge for anyone who caused an accidental death. Libnah was also given to them. Placing a city of refuge in the hands of the priests ensured that matters of justice and protection were handled with godly care.

The list of priestly cities continues with Jattir, Eshtemoa, Holon, Debir, Ain, Juttah, and Beth-shemesh, each with its surrounding pastures. These made nine cities in total taken from the territories of Judah and Simeon. Beth-shemesh would later become famous as the first town to receive the ark of the covenant when the Philistines returned it.

Benjamin provided four cities with their pastures: Gibeon, Geba, Anathoth, and Almon. Anathoth later became well known as the hometown of the prophet Jeremiah. Giving four towns was a very generous contribution from such a small tribe.

All together, Aaron's descendants were given thirteen cities with their pasturelands. This seemed like a very large grant for the small number of priests alive at the time. God was providing ahead of time for future generations as the priestly family grew in number.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars argue that this list reflects a much later period in Israel's history, because several of these towns were not fully occupied by Israel in Joshua's day.

notes.meaning: The rest of the Kohathite families, who were not from Aaron's priestly line, were given their towns next. They received their first allotment from the neighboring hill country of Ephraim. Moses' own descendants were included among these ordinary Levites without receiving any special rank.

Ephraim gave them four towns: Shechem, Gezer, Kibzaim, and Beth-horon, along with their pasturelands. Shechem was another city of refuge set on a mountain where it could be seen clearly from a distance. God ensured that safe havens and spiritual teachers were spread evenly across the central hills of the land.
